references.title: Choose your next EX200 practice task
references.body:
Use the linked public Red Hat EX200 objectives to check the scope of your preparation. For each row, attempt the work order from a fresh snapshot with new names or values. Record the command output that persuaded you and repeat persistent checks after reboot.

| Skill | Independent demonstration |
| --- | --- |
| Shell and files | Edit a log, extract matching records, redirect errors, test both link types, and restore a compressed archive. Find an unfamiliar flag offline. |
| Software | Add a trusted RPM source and a user Flatpak remote. Install, verify and remove a real package or app from each. |
| Scripting | Deliver a program handling empty input, a threshold boundary, multiple arguments and filenames with spaces. |
| Live systems | Identify a resource consumer, adjust its priority, change a TuneD profile, retain a journal across boots and retrieve a file over SSH. |
| Local storage | Add GPT, PV, VG, LV and swap capacity, prove earlier data survives growth and retire only practice storage. |
| Filesystems | Create and mount an ext4, XFS and VFAT volume individually, grow a supported filesystem, persist a mount and trigger an NFS mount. |
| Maintenance | Schedule one-shot and recurring work, configure chronyd, control units at boot and test one temporary and one persistent boot choice. |
| Networking | Activate a persistent dual-stack profile, resolve a private name and limit the permitted service in its interface zone. |
| Identity | Create and retire an account, modify supplementary groups, inspect password aging and delegate one exact command. |
| Security | Test file creation masks, key-based login, live and persistent firewall rules, file and process types, port labels and a policy Boolean. |

Save evidence, such as a fresh user login, a client request, a checksum or a later boot.

[Red Hat EX200 objectives](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex200-red-hat-certified-system-administrator-rhcsa-exam) · [RHEL 10 manuals](https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_enterprise_linux/10) · [Sequencing reference: Sander van Vugt’s RHEL 10 course outline](https://www.pearsonitcertification.com/store/red-hat-rhcsa-rhel-10-with-exam-labs-pearson-cert-prep-9780135493106)

references.title: Set up and reset the AlmaLinux 10.3 lab
references.body:
# AlmaLinux 10.3 practice lab for RHCSA and RHCE in Ansible

Use one official installer for both courses. The smaller **Erudior-setup.iso** in this kit is a second, read-only disc with the guest configuration scripts. The host launcher attaches both discs. Keep the four scripts and the setup disc together with **lab.py** after extracting the ZIP.

**Already using Erudior's graded RHCSA desktop exam?** Open the completed attempt, save its result, select **Reset exam disks**, then **Prepare machines** for a fresh attempt. Use **Begin** when ready for the timer. The desktop app supplies its own guest identities, exercises and isolated overlays. For automatic DVD and practice-kit setup, see **Graded desktop template** below. The host commands below manage the separate manual practice pair.

## 1. Get and verify the installation DVD

[Download AlmaLinux 10.3 x86_64 DVD ISO](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/10.3/isos/x86_64/AlmaLinux-10.3-x86_64-dvd.iso) · [Signed checksums](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/10.3/isos/x86_64/CHECKSUM) · [Release notes and signing fingerprint](https://wiki.almalinux.org/release-notes/10.3) · [AlmaLinux signing key](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/RPM-GPG-KEY-AlmaLinux-10)

Use the full DVD for the standard x86_64 architecture. It carries BaseOS and AppStream for the offline installation and package labs. Its exact size is **10,824,908,800 bytes**. The SHA-256 digest is **f74ae9c4a8e7e3e70147534856ea276f71649d16c70b7d3ec80d0905a7b93982**. The host launcher checks both before creating any lab disks.

The kit also includes the upstream signed CHECKSUM and public key. To inspect them with GnuPG from the kit directory on Linux:

`gpg` inspects keys and verifies signatures. A separate --homedir confines this exercise's key material to the chosen directory.

`sha256sum` calculates a digest from file contents. Matching digests let you check that the same bytes survived a copy or reboot.

Match the full primary fingerprint **EE6D B7B9 8F5B F5ED D9DA 0DE5 DEE5 C11C C2A1 E572** against the release notes. Look for a good signature, then match the computed digest to the exact DVD filename in CHECKSUM. If the distribution moves the point release to its archive, use an official AlmaLinux mirror with that same filename and digest.

## 2. Create the two manual guests

Use a Linux desktop host with Python 3.9+, QEMU system x86 with a graphical display, and qemu-img. On Fedora install `sudo dnf install python3 qemu-system-x86 qemu-img qemu-ui-gtk`.

On Debian install `sudo apt install python3 qemu-system-x86 qemu-system-gui qemu-utils`.

`apt` installs packages on a Debian-based host.

Windows users can run the Linux launcher inside a graphical WSL 2 distro with WSLg. Store its VM disks on the distro's Linux filesystem. On macOS the Erudior graded desktop route uses Lima. For this manual launcher use a graphical Linux VM with sufficient resources. KVM acceleration is used on eligible x86_64 hosts with accessible /dev/kvm. Software emulation uses QEMU's max CPU. Allow at least 8 GiB for the pair plus memory for the host and enough disk for the DVD, both installed systems, and a standalone copy at each saved baseline.

| Setting | Server | Client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Virtual CPU and memory | 2 vCPUs, 4 GiB | 2 vCPUs, 4 GiB |
| Install destination | 30 GiB system disk | 30 GiB system disk |
| Practice storage after installation | Two blank 2 GiB disks | Two blank 2 GiB disks |
| Private host address | 192.168.77.10/24 | 192.168.77.20/24 |
| RHCE role | Managed node | Ansible control node |
| Virtual network | Private link plus a separate NAT uplink | Same private link, independent NAT uplink |

The private link uses a loopback socket on host port 25763 for RHCSA or 25764 for RHCE. Guest traffic stays off the physical LAN. Port 25763/25764 must be free on the host. Use the local guest consoles. The launcher creates its disks inside **~/Erudior-Practice/rhcsa** or **~/Erudior-Practice/rhce**. Use one track at a time if memory is limited. Keep each track directory at its original path because qcow2 overlays reference absolute baseline paths.

From the extracted kit directory on the host, substitute **rhce** for **rhcsa** throughout if building the automation pair.

In the installer choose **Minimal Install**, automatic partitioning of the single 30 GiB disk, a local user **learner**, a password you choose, and **administrator** membership. Complete installation and reboot from the system disk. Leave the server VM running for the client’s private-network connection. If you closed it, use the terminal session first.

With the server running, start the client installer on the host.

Make the same installation choices on the client. After both installations, power off both from their consoles with `sudo systemctl poweroff`.

Use the terminal session on the host.

This normal boot attaches both storage-practice disks to each machine and starts the server before the client. Only the system disk was present during installation.

## 3. Configure and check the guests

At each guest console, as learner, mount the supplied setup disc. The installer DVD stays attached for packages. The setup script selects the private NIC by the MAC assigned by the launcher.

Choose the profile that matches this pair. Run each command on the named guest.

For offline RHCE web-package labs, set the playbook repository base URL to `file:///mnt/erudior-dvd/{{ item }}/` on the managed server. Keep the exercise’s repository IDs, signing key, GPG checks and explicit repository selection. The installed DVD supplies both the catalogs and signed RPMs.

Both profiles enable SSH, the firewall and chrony, use AlmaLinux's trusted key for RPM packages, and require enforcing SELinux. The course DVD repositories are disabled by default and explicitly selected for setup. On later offline package exercises use `sudo dnf --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo='erudior-dvd-*' list --available`.

The guest mounts the attached installer DVD on demand after reboot.

**RHCSA.** The server supplies a read-only NFS marker restricted to the client and an initially stopped, disabled maintenance unit. The client has an empty repository catalog for the repository exercise. The practice disks, learner account tasks, automount configuration, storage layouts and service-repair work are left for the learner. After both machines are configured run `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhcsa server` on the server and `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhcsa client` on the client.

The client check mounts and reads the actual NFS export, then unmounts it.

**RHCE.** From the server console display the fingerprint with `sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`.

As **learner on the client**, use the terminal session, compare the fingerprint when prompted, and enter the credentials you chose.

The helper creates or reuses the dedicated learner key, verifies the remote hostname, runs an Ansible ping and requests sudo to confirm UID 0. It ends the temporary SSH agent. Run `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhce server` and `sudo bash /mnt/erudior-tools/check-guest.sh rhce client` on the corresponding guests.

For the Navigator and editor practicals, keep NAT online during one-time preparation. As **learner on the RHCE client**, use the terminal session.

This stages the course’s pinned Navigator version, rootless Podman execution image and development image, then executes Ansible in the locally stored runtime. Open the course’s VS Code Dev Containers workspace once while online to stage the editor components and establish the workspace mounts. Use the course's **Identify the Ansible runtime** and **Author and run an inspection play in VS Code** lessons to verify the actual editor and playbook workflow. Retain the previous unit's inputs when capturing a later practical's baseline. Red Hat uses RHEL 10 for EX200 and Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform for EX294. These are Erudior practice profiles.

## 4. Capture once and reset for each attempt

Reboot once and confirm the expected private addresses, SELinux state and peer access. Remount the setup disc to run the checks again if needed. Save your baseline **after preparation and before solving the test**. At each guest console use `sudo systemctl poweroff`.

On the **host**, run the command for your track:

For your **next fresh attempt** use one host command:

Reset gracefully powers off any running guests on that track, switches all six disks to fresh overlays of the saved baseline as one operation, and optionally starts the pair. `--offline` restricts the new guests' NAT uplinks and keeps their private connection. Omit it for lessons that need external downloads. Without `--start`, the reset pair stays off. Changes since capture are discarded, including guest-local Git commits and assessment evidence. Save work you want to keep outside the VMs first. After a cold boot, reload any passphrase-protected key into your terminal’s SSH agent. The key and its trust records on disk return with the baseline.

A **named baseline** is useful when a practical starts partway through the course. For the RHCE web promotion, first complete the blue deployment, run the blue endpoint checker, and shut down both guests. Then use:

Reusing an existing capture name is refused. Resetting one track leaves the other track and all saved baselines alone. If a broken guest cannot handle ACPI shutdown, `python3 lab.py reset rhce --force-off --start --offline` requests an immediate power-off of that track’s disposable VMs before restoring them. Use the correct track and baseline name. The launcher refuses a reset when no such baseline exists. A preparation failure leaves the current disk set selected. Close any external program that has opened a practice disk before retrying.

## Graded desktop template

In Erudior Desktop, open **Open practice terminal** from the first reading or open a practical and expand **First-time setup**. The desktop provider can build the shared base directly from the verified AlmaLinux DVD and practice kit. For local copies, use **Choose DVD ISO** and **Choose practice kit ZIP**. If media are missing, starting preparation can fetch them. Leave the provider running during the installation. The resulting private base supplies fresh client and server disks for each new attempt. From a reading use **Start lab**. In a timed practical use **Prepare machines** and then **Begin** when you want the clock to start.

The Linux host commands above manage the standalone kit's manual pair. The app's **Reset disks** action resets the shared practice pair. A completed practical has its own **Reset exam disks** action. Save the result before resetting an assessment. The two reset controls have different targets, so check the course and lesson on screen before choosing one.

[Red Hat EX200 objectives](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex200-red-hat-certified-system-administrator-rhcsa-exam) · [Red Hat EX294 objectives](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex294-red-hat-certified-engineer-rhce-exam-red-hat-enterprise-linux)

## Terminal session

Choose one host distribution and one course profile. Run lab.py on the host. Preparation and readiness checks belong in the guest named by their last argument. Each capture or reset is a separate choice. Save work before resetting. The final forced reset is only for a stalled RHCE pair that cannot power off gracefully. Read the instructions above before choosing steps.

references.title: Your route from first login to the practical
references.body:
Start with **Meet Linux and install your first practice machine**. You can begin with no command-line experience. Each stage below ends with work to do from a blank prompt. Use local documentation freely. When you can explain the observed result and repeat it using new names or values, move on.

| Stage | Work through | Show you can do it unaided |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Find your footing | The first three lessons, Bash arguments and offline help | Identify client and server, recover from an unfinished command, then discover a flag in a local manual and test it. |
| 2. Handle real files | Paths, links, editing, streams, log patterns, archives and permissions | Finish **Independent shift: restore an operator's handoff** in a fresh directory. Hand another operator a restored archive they can verify. |
| 3. Give people access | User identities, login contexts, account aging, groups and shared files | Log in with fresh group membership. Demonstrate both permitted and denied access as the affected account and complete the team-directory and operator practicals. |
| 4. Bring two machines online | Address plans, saved NetworkManager profiles and hostname lookup | Choose the correct interface for an address, configure both protocol families on a practice profile and make the server discoverable from the client. |
| 5. Supply software | Repository metadata, signed RPM transactions and user-scoped Flatpak | Install a known signed package from the DVD, identify its owner and remove it. Install the offline inventory payload from your own signed Flatpak remote and restore the prior user state. |
| 6. Operate a shift | CPU and memory, process signals, tuning, journal history, services, schedules and time | Diagnose a failed scheduled service, make it work again after boot and explain whether the time client has selected a source. |
| 7. Automate a repeated decision | Bash arguments, loops, result codes and the executable classifier | Write a script and test absent input, a filename containing a space, an empty file and a mixed success/failure case. |
| 8. Extend and mount storage | GPT, LVM, swap, filesystem types, mount identity, NFS and autofs | Extend a volume while preserving its marker. Verify a persistent mount after reboot and demonstrate that an on-demand file actually comes from the server. |
| 9. Diagnose and secure a server | Boot entries, targets, recovery, SSH, firewall zones, HTTP and SELinux | Distinguish a missing listener, a blocked route to a listening service, ordinary access failure and a label mismatch. Repeat the client request after the smallest correction. |
| 10. Work independently | Both rehearsals, the untimed branch-archive work order, the three-hour mock and the after-action review | Repeat the problem areas from fresh disks, without a worked example open. Keep evidence from before and after the reboot. |

## How to use a worked lesson

Read a command and predict one line you expect to see. Run it in the named guest. If the output differs, record the exact account, host and path before changing anything. Use the final ticket to practice the same decision with different inputs. The two shift assignments include worked reviews and observable self-checks. A quiz checks reasoning. A desktop practical separately records machine state. Write down both when they disagree.

For instance, being able to define a symbolic link can earn a quiz answer. Recovering a portable link inside a restored handoff directory demonstrates that you can apply the idea. A later integrated assignment should ask for the result without naming the command to use.

## Exam scope and course extension

The core course follows Red Hat's published RHEL 10 EX200 study points. The built-in mock samples ten outcomes. Use **Choose your next EX200 practice task** alongside the mock result to cover skills that one attempt cannot sample, including Flatpak, regular expressions, both IP versions, local documentation, filesystem types, alternate boot selections and SELinux controls. The entitled RHEL CDN exercise uses a registered RHEL system. The AlmaLinux guest uses its signed DVD sources for the local equivalent.

Sander van Vugt's public RHEL 10 outline was used to review the progression from everyday administration through recovery, network services and a sample exam. The optional container workshop comes after the exam review. Its Podman and image-mode material is enrichment beyond the current public EX200 task list. All practice tickets and answer explanations here are Erudior exercises.

[Official EX200 objectives](https://www.redhat.com/en/services/training/ex200-red-hat-certified-system-administrator-rhcsa-exam) · [Pearson's public RHEL 10 course outline](https://www.informit.com/store/red-hat-rhcsa-rhel-10-with-exam-labs-pearson-cert-prep-9780135493106)

references.title: Make the offline Flatpak practice shelf
references.body:
Use this once on a fresh untimed client as learner. The setup requires Bash, Flatpak and GnuPG (gpg or gpg2). It produces the small runtime, inventory payload, local repository and public key for the Flatpak lesson. The script signs the shelf locally and discards its temporary private key. Keep the public key with the repository so you can repeat the installation.

The session writes **make-shelf.sh** and runs it as learner.

A successful last line reports the shelf location. The application is a small data payload for practicing package management. Look for its inventory document in the installed deployment.

## Terminal session

```plaintext
>cat > make-shelf.sh <<'ERUDIOR_FILE'
>#!/bin/bash
>set -eu
>shelf="$HOME/rhcsa-flatpak-shelf"
>if test -e "$shelf"; then
>    echo "Choose an unused shelf directory before starting." >&2
>    exit 1
>fi
>arch=$(flatpak --default-arch)
>mkdir -p "$shelf/runtime/files" "$shelf/runtime/usr/share" "$shelf/app/files/share"
>keys=$(mktemp -d)
>trap 'gpgconf --homedir "$keys" --kill gpg-agent || true; rm -rf -- "$keys"' EXIT
>gpg --homedir "$keys" --batch --pinentry-mode loopback --passphrase '' --quick-gen-key 'RHCSA disposable shelf <shelf@example.invalid>' rsa2048 sign 0
>key=$(gpg --homedir "$keys" --with-colons --list-secret-keys | awk -F: '$1=="fpr"{print $10; exit}')
>gpg --homedir "$keys" --export "$key" > "$shelf/shelf.gpg"
>ref="org.erudior.ShelfPlatform/$arch/stable"
>printf '[Runtime]\nname=org.erudior.ShelfPlatform\nruntime=%s\nsdk=%s\n' "$ref" "$ref" > "$shelf/runtime/metadata"
>printf '[Application]\nname=org.erudior.ShelfNotes\nruntime=%s\nsdk=%s\n' "$ref" "$ref" > "$shelf/app/metadata"
>printf 'Offline practice runtime\n' > "$shelf/runtime/usr/share/shelf.txt"
>printf 'Inventory sheet\n' > "$shelf/app/files/share/inventory.txt"
>flatpak build-finish "$shelf/app"
>flatpak build-export --runtime --gpg-sign="$key" --gpg-homedir="$keys" "$shelf/repo" "$shelf/runtime" stable
>flatpak build-export --gpg-sign="$key" --gpg-homedir="$keys" "$shelf/repo" "$shelf/app" stable
>flatpak build-update-repo --gpg-sign="$key" --gpg-homedir="$keys" "$shelf/repo"
>printf 'Shelf ready at %s\n' "$shelf"
>ERUDIOR_FILE

>bash make-shelf.sh
Shelf ready at /home/learner/rhcsa-flatpak-shelf
```

references.title: Build a tiny practice image from the guest
references.body:
Use the optional workshop on the untimed x86-64 AlmaLinux client. Check `command -v podman`.

If it is absent on the kit guest, use `sudo dnf --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=erudior-dvd-baseos,erudior-dvd-appstream install podman`.

Log in as learner and use the terminal session.

This exercise uses a local shell already shipped on that guest. The image has Bash's shell builtins and its shared libraries. It needs no registry and contains no package manager. Check that `localhost/rhcsa-shell:practice` is an unused local tag. Save the following file as build-shell-image.sh in the learner account.

Run the saved builder from the directory containing the file.

The image includes only the shell, its interpreter and its dynamic dependencies. Keep the tag while you complete the optional lesson. After removing its practice containers, remove this image with `podman rmi localhost/rhcsa-shell:practice`.

## Terminal session

```plaintext
>command -v podman
/usr/bin/podman
>sudo dnf --disablerepo='*' --enablerepo=erudior-dvd-baseos,erudior-dvd-appstream install podman
Transaction Summary
Is this ok [y/N]:
>podman info
host:
  arch: amd64
  os: linux
>cat > build-shell-image.sh <<'ERUDIOR_FILE'
>#!/bin/bash
>set -eu
>work=$(mktemp -d)
>mkdir "$work/root"
>install -D -m 0755 /bin/sh "$work/root/bin/sh"
>ldd /bin/sh | awk '$3 ~ /^\// {print $3} $1 ~ /^\// {print $1}' > "$work/libs"
>while IFS= read -r lib; do
>    install -D -m 0755 "$lib" "$work/root$lib"
>done < "$work/libs"
>mkdir -p "$work/root/ledger" "$work/root/tmp"
>chmod 1777 "$work/root/tmp"
>tar --numeric-owner --owner=0 --group=0 -cf "$work/shell.tar" -C "$work/root" .
>podman import "$work/shell.tar" localhost/rhcsa-shell:practice
>podman run --pull=never --rm localhost/rhcsa-shell:practice /bin/sh -c 'printf "Local shell ready\n"'
>ERUDIOR_FILE

>bash build-shell-image.sh
Local shell ready
>image=localhost/rhcsa-shell:practice

>podman rmi localhost/rhcsa-shell:practice
Untagged: localhost/rhcsa-shell:practice
```

glossary.definition: The part of Linux that manages hardware, memory, processes and system calls.
An interpreter that expands the words you type and runs commands.
The directory from which a process resolves relative paths.
The small numeric result a process returns to its caller. Zero conventionally means success.
A filesystem record describing an object. Multiple hard-linked names refer to the same inode.
The directory where a filesystem is attached to the visible directory tree.
An identifier stored with a filesystem or other volume so it can be recognized across device-name changes.
A pool of storage extents contributed by physical volumes.
A block device allocated from a volume group. A filesystem can be created on it.
A published collection of software and the metadata a package manager uses to find it.
A numeric process identifier on one running machine.
An object managed by systemd, such as a service, timer or mount.
A systemd unit grouping other units into a desired system state.
A communication endpoint. A listening network socket has an address, transport and port.
The number of leading address bits describing a network prefix.
The context field commonly used by policy rules to govern interactions between a process and an object.
Bits removed from permissions requested when a process creates a file or directory.
An identifier for the current kernel boot, useful for separating observations across restarts.
One value passed to a program after the shell expands the command line.
In Flatpak, a separately installed set of software shared by compatible applications.
A number the kernel assigns to a running process.
A partition table recording the ranges allocated to partitions on a block device.
A packaged starting filesystem and configuration from which a container can be created.
